quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: As your motorcycle speeds up, you need to:

options.text: Shift to a higher gear.
Shift to a lower gear.
Put the bike in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a higher gear.
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle speeds up, shift into a higher gear.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same location as your motorcycle.
Take it right out on the highway.
Learn how it works in a safe, controlled area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Learn how it works in a safe, controlled area first.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, find all the controls and practice in a safe area. Get used to how it handles before riding on the road.

questions.question: When taking a curve while riding in a group, ride in:

options.text: Single file.
Pairs.
Staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Single file.
questions.explanation: Groups normally ride in staggered formation. Switch to single file when taking a curve, making a turn, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Motorcycles are allowed to:

options.text: Use a full lane without sharing it.
Share a lane with a car.
Share a lane with a small truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a full lane without sharing it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use a full traffic lane. Other drivers cannot prevent motorcyclists from using an entire lane.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Only stop if other traffic is coming.
Vehicles will enter the roadway soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to all traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, ride in which part of your lane?

options.text: The left portion
The center portion
The right portion

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This improves your view ahead and helps drivers in the next lane see your move.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road shows:

options.text: No parking allowed.
The right edge of a traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: If you see a hazard in the road, do not:

options.text: Alert other drivers.
Change your speed if needed.
Use your horn, lights, or signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alert other drivers.
questions.explanation: Always tell other drivers you are there. Use your horn, lights, and signals. Adjust your speed and lane position as needed to stay safe.

questions.question: Which of these affects a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
The drinker's height
The temperature outside

questions.correctAnswerText: The amount of alcohol consumed
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: how much alcohol was consumed, how fast it was consumed, and the drinker's body weight.

questions.question: Before riding, check your clutch. It should feel:

options.text: Loose and rough.
Tight and smooth.
Loose and smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tight and smooth.
questions.explanation: Check your clutch and throttle before riding. The throttle should snap back when released, and the clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: To tell other riders that you are near them.
To help other drivers see your motorcycle in slow traffic.
To warn other drivers you are slowing down or stopping unexpectedly.

questions.correctAnswerText: To warn other drivers you are slowing down or stopping unexpectedly.
questions.explanation: Use your brake light to communicate with other drivers. Flash your brake light before slowing down for sharp turns on highways or whenever other drivers may not expect you to slow down.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the signal will change to red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through it.

questions.question: What type of boots or shoes should a rider wear?

options.text: Boots or shoes below the ankles.
Boots or shoes that cover the ankles.
Boots or shoes made of soft material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Boots or shoes that cover the ankles.
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy footwear that covers and supports your ankles. The soles should be made of hard, durable material that resists slipping.

questions.question: How should you approach a blind intersection?

options.text: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
Skip the stop line and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop line and then proceed through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop line or sign. Then carefully move forward and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward to look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: What should you do when railroad crossing lights are flashing?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Proceed with caution.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with flashing lights, come to a complete stop. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before going forward. Never try to drive across the tracks before a train.

questions.question: How can you make it easier for others to see you?

options.text: Wear brightly-colored clothing while riding.
Wear dark-colored clothing while riding.
Wave your arms while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear brightly-colored clothing while riding.
questions.explanation: Wearing bright colors makes you visible to other drivers at any time of day.

questions.question: What is true about operating a motorized scooter?

options.text: You can only operate it during the day.
You do not need a driver license.
You can operate it with any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can operate it with any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any class of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.

questions.question: How much stopping distance do motorcycles need?

options.text: Less stopping distance than larger vehicles.
The same stopping distance as larger vehicles.
They can stop instantly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same stopping distance as larger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need as much stopping distance as other vehicles. Always keep enough space between you and other vehicles based on road conditions.

questions.question: Your motorcycle starts to weave on bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to cross the surface faster.
Ride in a zigzag pattern.
Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves on bridge gratings, maintain a steady speed and go straight across. Do not try to swerve side to side, as this is dangerous.

questions.question: Is it safe to ride directly alongside another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, because you are in a separate lane.
Yes, because it blocks the wind.
No, because you may be in the driver's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because you may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride alongside other vehicles. You may be in a driver's blind spot, and they could move into your lane without seeing you.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle provides the most stopping power?

options.text: The front brake
The rear brake
The emergency brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of a motorcycle's stopping power. Use both brakes every time you stop.

questions.question: When choosing a riding jacket, it should:

options.text: Fit loosely and flap in the wind.
Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
Not be made of leather or sturdy material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants made of leather or sturdy material. They should fit snugly enough to not flap in the wind, but loose enough to let you move freely.

questions.question: When should you use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch?

options.text: The throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
You start to lose control in a curve.
The motorcycle starts to wobble.

questions.correctAnswerText: The throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
questions.explanation: If the throttle gets stuck and you cannot free it, immediately use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch. This removes power from the rear wheel so you can safely stop.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Ride within the posted speed limits.
Exceed the speed limit by up to 10 mph to complete the pass.
Pass more than one vehicle at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride within the posted speed limits.
questions.explanation: Complete all passes within legal speed limits. Pass only where it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while stopping, you should:

options.text: Continue to apply the front brake.
Release the front brake and only use the rear brake.
Release the front brake immediately, then apply it firmly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately, then apply it firmly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while stopping, release the front brake right away and then apply it firmly again. Use both brakes if you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: In a crash, a rider wearing a helmet is:

options.text: Less likely to survive than someone without a helmet.
Just as likely to survive as someone without a helmet.
More likely to survive than someone without a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: More likely to survive than someone without a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries than riders wearing helmets, regardless of speed.

questions.question: To reduce the chance of a crash, you should:

options.text: Not use turn signals.
Use proper lane positions.
Follow other vehicles closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use proper lane positions.
questions.explanation: To reduce crashes, stay visible, signal your intentions, keep safe distance, look ahead at least 12 seconds, identify hazards, and be ready to react to changes.

questions.question: Lanes moving in the same direction are separated by:

options.text: White lines.
Yellow lines.
Road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid lines mean no passing. Dashed lines mean passing is allowed if it is safe.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: Stop completely.
Proceed through the intersection with caution.
Yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop completely and wait for a signal that allows you to turn in your direction.

questions.question: When being passed, you should ride in:

options.text: The left portion of the lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding near the passing driver increases collision risk. Riding far away may tempt them to return to your lane too soon.
